claims.text: High-thermal-load LPBF of AlCrFeNiSi typically produces steep thermal gradients, significant residual stresses, and microstructural heterogeneity.
A 50 µs pulse with a 150 µs dwell time represents an approximately 30% reduction in pulse duration.
Pulse-modulated laser scanning with reduced pulse duration and tailored inter-pulse dwell time will induce nonequilibrium chemical short-range order in AlCrFeNiSi during solidification.
Rapid solidification can establish nonequilibrium chemical short-range-order states.
Reduced energy per pulse and extended dwell times lower thermal gradients during solidification.
Lower thermal gradients promote a more uniform atomic arrangement through nonequilibrium SRO formation at grain boundaries.
SRO-mediated atomic uniformity at grain boundaries alleviates localized residual stresses.
Reducing thermal input can reduce microstructural defects associated with high thermal loads.
Pulse-modulated processing will produce lower residual stresses than conventional continuous high-energy scanning.
Pulse-modulated processing will improve yield strength relative to conventional continuous high-energy scanning.
Pulse-modulated processing will improve fatigue strength relative to conventional continuous high-energy scanning.
Pulse-modulated processing will produce a more homogenized microstructure than conventional continuous high-energy scanning.
Standard high-energy continuous laser scanning produces high thermal gradients, residual stresses, and microstructural heterogeneity.
The proposed regime is applicable to sub-centimeter AlCrFeNiSi components made by LPBF under ambient build-chamber conditions.
The effectiveness of the proposed regime for larger components or alternative manufacturing parameters is not established.
The pulse and dwell times required to reproducibly induce the desired SRO are difficult to tune precisely.
The influence of induced SRO on all relevant mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi remains insufficiently quantified.
